preamble: The postalveolar ejective affricate [tʃʼ] is replaced by the voiced palatal implosive [ʄ]. Konso (Lowland East Cushitic) has no ejectives but has four implosives, ɓ ɗ ʄ ʛ. Orkaydo (2013: 8) describes a systematic correspondence in loans from Amharic: the palatal ejective (his cʼ, Amharic [tʃʼ]) becomes ʄ, just as kʼ becomes ʛ and pʼ becomes ɓ (Amharic tʼərəpʼpʼezza > Konso taraɓɓeessaa 'table'), whereas tʼ and sʼ become plain t and s. The evidence is loanword adaptation in a single language, with two words, so certainty is 2. No inherited Konso ʄ < *tʃʼ correspondence was verified.
phoneticEffects: Implosivization, Voicing, Deaffrication, Airstream Change, Loanword Adaptation

examples.note: Orkaydo (2013: 8). The final kʼ becomes ʛ in the same word.

sources: Orkaydo, O. O. (2013). A Grammar of Konso. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LOT Dissertation Series). https://hdl.handle.net/1887/20681
